Unlike older eras where major criminal figures operated openly and attracted global attention, today’s structures function in a far more discreet and complex way. The individuals behind these networks rarely appear in the spotlight. Instead, they operate through layers of intermediaries, legal businesses, and international logistics systems that make detection extremely difficult.

The film takes a deep look into how these covert networks are built, how they expand across continents, and how they manage to remain hidden within everyday global commerce. It highlights the transformation of organized crime from visible hierarchies into decentralized and highly adaptive systems.

The documentary also shows how international enforcement agencies attempt to track and dismantle these hidden operations, often facing significant challenges due to their complexity and scale.

snippet.title: The Most Dangerous Soccer Match Ever Played
snippet.description:
Reconstructing the tragic game between the forced labourers of Ukrainian team ‘FC Start’ and the team of the German Air Force ‘Flakelf’, ‘The Fatal Eleven’ tells the story about soccer and Nazism, about courage and power, about red jerseys and the fatal consequences of a 5-3 victory.

It was much more than just a soccer match, when on the 9th of August 1942 the ‘FC Start’, the Ukrainian workers of the ‘3rd bakery unit’, entered the pitch of the Zenit stadium in Kiev to play against ‘Flakelf’, the team of the German Air Force, everybody in the Zenit Stadium knew what they were playing for. The spectator stands were packed with people.

A year before, on the 19th of September 1941 the German Wehrmacht marched into Kiev. Within two days Nazi regime murdered nearly 34.000 Jews. 630.000 Soviet soldiers became prisoners of war. The deportation of Jews and Ukrainian forced labourers to Germany was running at full steam. The citizens of Kiev were starving. No one could think about playing soccer under such appalling conditions. Yet, no one forgot this sport.
What the Nazis could not know: hidden behind the bakery forced labourer’s team were some of the best soccer players of Dynamo Kiev, the leading Soviet soccer club, and of his local rival club Lokomotive. Both clubs were officially banned from the soccer all league in the Nazi occupied territories. But the “FC Start” was allowed to compete with some garrison and soldier teams. The soccer matches were meant to pretend business as usual in wartime.
Soccer was supposed to cover Nazi disposal with sportive humanity. The ‘FC Start’ club with his Dynamo Kiev champions was determined to play to win. No one on the pitch could imagine what a victory of the suppressed ones would lead to. ‘The Fatal Eleven’ tells the true story of a very special match.

snippet.title: The Man Who Was Too Scared To Call For Help! | Abused By My Girlfriend
snippet.description:
"Violence has no gender. It doesn’t matter whether a victim is a woman or a man, their pain is the same."

In this video, you will witness one of the most disturbing and widely discussed domestic abuse cases in the history of the United Kingdom. At just 21 years old, Alex Skeel was isolated for years, starved, subjected to severe physical abuse, and repeatedly harmed by his girlfriend Jordan Worth, who appeared outwardly "polite, educated, and loving."

We hear Alex Skeel’s own account, along with police records, of how psychological manipulation (coercive control), clothing restrictions, and social isolation gradually escalated into a life-threatening situation. Medical reports reveal that if police had not intervened at the last moment, Alex’s life would have been in extreme danger within a short time.

Today, Alex Skeel is a survivor who speaks out to raise awareness that men can also be victims of domestic abuse, to give a voice to silent victims, and to explain how to recognize the early signs of abuse, sharing his story in full detail.
